audit.why: Chart already reads Karma / Karma / Skill / Karma / Ambessa / Skill / Karma in both layers and both layers agree row for row, matching the mirror and the packet chart.
audit.corrected: Left the chart alone; rewrote the phase whys that were still template text so each row says why it is where it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why says only 'his spike is the danger window' and never names Public Execution; the level-6 dip for Karma is stated in content but not in the full layer.
audit.why: Mantra is available at level 1, so Karma gains nothing at 6, while Public Execution (130/115/100s) blinks to the farthest champion in a line, suppresses, then stuns.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Ambessa's: Public Execution suppresses through everything except a shield already spent, and its 130s rank-1 cooldown is Karma's window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer invents an ability called 'Dash Chain' in twelve places; Ambessa has no such ability. Neither layer states what Repudiation (W) does to poke.
audit.why: Her passive is Drakehound's Step — a dash triggered by entering an attack or movement command during a cast, granting a bonus-range empowered attack. Repudiation shields and braces, and deals INCREASED damage if it blocked non-minion damage while bracing, so poking into the brace feeds it.
audit.corrected: Named Drakehound's Step and Public Execution in the full layer, added the tell (the empowered attack wind-up, not the spell cast), and stated that poking into a braced Repudiation increases her slam damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer is written in first person ('I open', 'my empowerment', 'she catches me').
audit.why: Breaks the second-person coaching voice used across the site.
audit.corrected: whys[0..6], early, mid and late converted to second person at matched length.

edits.before: Mantra is live from Level 1, so I open this lane, not her — the second she steps up to last-hit I drop RQ Soulflare on her, and the delayed zone slows and burns her before she has a dash charge banked to weave out. Levels 2-3 I layer Inner Flame poke on top, and Gathering Fire refunds my Mantra cooldown every time I tag her, so the empowerment rebuilds fast for the next RQ. The one thing to respect: she only needs one clean dash-into-W to open a trade, so I keep Inspire ready to shield-and-speed away rather than burning it on a poke step, and I never throw Inner Flame from inside her dash range.
edits.after: Mantra is live from Level 1, so you open this lane, not her — the second she steps up to last-hit drop RQ Soulflare on her, and the delayed zone slows and burns her before Drakehound's Step can weave her out. Levels 2-3 layer Inner Flame poke on top, and Gathering Fire refunds your Mantra cooldown every time you tag her, so the empowerment rebuilds fast for the next RQ. The one thing to respect: she only needs one clean dash into Repudiation to open a trade, so keep Inspire ready to shield-and-speed away, and never poke into the brace — blocked damage makes her slam hit harder.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my bullying peak — multiple Q into RQ Soulflare rotations shove her off the wave and let me tax plates behind Inspire's speed, and any greedy dash step-up gets tethered by Focused Resolve so the root lands before her W damage does. Level 6 is the dip, not a spike, for me: my R is just re-empowerment I already had access to since Level 1, while her actual ultimate plus a dash-stacked combo and chain CC close the range gap the moment my Inspire or RQ is down. So at 6 I stop poking on a hair-trigger and hold Inspire purely to peel her engage — if she catches me locked before I can shield, that's the trade she wins.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your bullying peak — Q into RQ Soulflare rotations shove her off the wave and let you tax plates behind Inspire's speed, and any greedy dash step-up gets tethered by Focused Resolve so the root lands before Repudiation's slam does. Level 6 is the dip, not a spike, for you: your R is re-empowerment you have had since Level 1, while Public Execution blinks, suppresses and stuns the moment your Inspire or RQ is down. So at 6 stop poking on a hair-trigger and hold Inspire purely to peel her engage — if she catches you locked before you shield, that's the trade she wins.

edits.before: When my first AP/haste item lands I get sharper RQ burst and a fatter Inspire shield, but it isn't a clean spike — she's hitting her first bruiser item the same window, so it nets out even and my job is to trade the tempo for shoves and roams, not all-ins. The honest truth is I have no late power spike of my own: by full items she's a stat-checking fighter who weaves my skillshots and outlasts a thin frame, so I need to have already snowballed this lead. I win by converting the early-to-first-item edge into plates, kills, and roams before her bruiser scaling lets her eat my poke and run me down on a single dash chain.
edits.after: When your first AP/haste item lands you get sharper RQ burst and a fatter Inspire shield, but it isn't a clean spike — she hits her first bruiser item the same window, so it nets out even and your job is to trade the tempo for shoves and roams, not all-ins. The honest truth is you have no late power spike of your own: by full items she is a stat-checking fighter who weaves your skillshots and outlasts a thin frame, so the lead has to already exist. Convert the early-to-first-item edge into plates, kills and roams before her bruiser scaling lets her eat your poke and run you down.
